audit_findings.title: Preferred-stock dividends are missing from the common-equity claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $301.875 million annual preferred dividend, equal to 19.6% of the $1,539.6 million OE anchor; dividend-settlement dilution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation uses a fully diluted share denominator reflecting preferred conversion, but projected common-equity OE must also bear preferred dividends until conversion or include every additional share issued to settle those dividends.
audit_findings.evidence: Dividends on the Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock will be payable on a cumulative basis when, as and if declared by our Board of Directors, or an authorized committee thereof, at an annual rate of 7.00 % on the liquidation preference of $ 1,000 per share.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual 7% cumulative claim on the $4.3125 billion liquidation preference is demonstrated. The supplied valuation shows no explicit deduction for the full dividend run-rate, while FY2026 contained only $13.088 million because the preferred stock was issued near year-end. Whether the operating PV otherwise incorporates the future dividends is unresolved, but the visible numerator-denominator mismatch is large enough to affect value materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every projected preferred dividend from the valuation date through conversion against OE, then rerun all scenarios using either cash deductions or the exact incremental shares under each stock-settlement and accumulated-dividend path.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved enforcement liabilities could rank ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Fines, disgorgement and defense costs would reduce OE or the equity bridge; denial of export privileges could also reduce normalized OE and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has not been informed that it is the target of any of these investigations to date, but if we become the target of any of these investigations, the Department of Justice could pursue civil or criminal enforcement actions against us, seek monetary or other penalties from us (including disgorgement), or require changes to our compliance program and internal controls.
audit_findings.explanation: Ongoing SEC, DOJ and BIS matters are demonstrated, but the company had not been identified as a target and disclosed no estimable loss range. No liability or operating impairment is therefore demonstrated. Potential consequences could be material, but the supplied record cannot establish their probability or amount.
audit_findings.action: Obtain post-filing investigation status, counsel's probability and loss-range assessment, applicable insurance limits and exclusions, compliance-cost forecasts, and a quantified export-privilege suspension scenario before rerunning value.

audit_findings.title: Cash treated as excess may instead fund enormous purchase commitments
audit_findings.magnitude: $7,521.474 million bridge exposure, equal to $8.00 per diluted share and 25.8% of base equity value; $34.2 billion commitments equal 4.55 times cash; FY2026 operating cash outflow was $6,809.886 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for working capital, pledged balances or commitment performance is operating cash and must be excluded from the excess-cash bridge; commitment losses or inventory write-downs would also reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of June 30, 2026, these remaining non-cancelable commitments were $ 34.2 billion, including $ 0.2 billion for related parties.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitments do not themselves prove a loss because some may be supported by customer orders, deposits or price protection. However, adding 100% of cash as excess is unsupported by the supplied matching evidence, particularly with $12.896 billion of inventory, $6.125 billion of receivables and substantial operating cash consumption. The entire cash add is large enough to change the valuation materially even if only part proves operationally required.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a commitment-by-commitment match to enforceable customer orders, deposits, cancellation rights and supplier protections; calculate minimum operating and pledged cash under cancellation and margin stresses; rerun the bridge using only the evidenced excess amount.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may not contain a full-year recurring interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 interest expense of $194.574 million, equal to 12.6% of the OE anchor, including $83.0 million of additional expense from second-half revolver drawdowns; pro-forma shortfall unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is equity-level OE, recurring interest, commitment fees and debt-cost amortization reduce the OE numerator rather than the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The $135.0 million or 226.5% increase in interest expense was primarily driven by a $58.6 million or 160.5% increase in interest and amortization related to the amendment of the 2029 Convertible Notes and new issuance of the 2028 Convertible Notes and the 2030 Convertible Notes during the second half of fiscal 2025, as well as $83.0 million additional interest expense related to the drawdown on our revolving credit facilities during the second half of fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation's retention of interest expense is methodologically coherent, but the $1,539.6 million trend anchor spans years before the June 2026 debt structure was fully outstanding. A missing full-year burden is not demonstrated without a pro-forma schedule, yet the filed interest amounts are sufficiently large relative to anchor OE to make the issue reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Construct contractual pro-forma interest, fee and amortization schedules using June 2026 balances and rates, reconcile them to the $194.574 million reported expense, and rerun all scenarios with the recurring after-tax difference reflected in OE.

audit_findings.title: After-tax earnings rely on an unapproved Malaysian incentive
audit_findings.mechanism: Failure or limitation of the incentive would increase recurring cash taxes and reduce after-tax OE; changes to the effective tax burden could also affect sustainable growth economics.
audit_findings.evidence: Our effective tax rate also reflects our expectation that future income generated by our Malaysian subsidiary will substantially benefit from a Malaysian government tax incentive program for which we have applied but have not yet received final approval.
audit_findings.explanation: Reliance on an incentive lacking final approval is demonstrated, and management states that its effective tax rate reflects the expected benefit. However, Malaysian taxable income, the modeled benefit and the effect of Pillar Two are not separately quantified, so the record cannot establish the valuation impact's materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the application decision and evidence that the December 2026 investment condition was satisfied; calculate Malaysian cash taxes with no incentive and under the 15% minimum-tax framework; rerun OE using each supported tax case.

audit_findings.title: The source earnings remain exposed to a material IT-control weakness
audit_findings.mechanism: A resulting misstatement could affect the OE numerator and growth history through revenue, expenses or working capital, alter diluted shares or liabilities, and change the amount of cash classified as excess in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s information technology controls for certain systems that support some of the financial reporting processes did not operate for a sufficient period of time, and the Company did not perform controls in a consistent and timely manner to monitor user access to certain financial applications, system infrastructure and programs.
audit_findings.explanation: The IT-control material weakness and adverse ICFR opinion are demonstrated, but no financial-statement misstatement is demonstrated. BDO issued an unqualified financial-statement opinion after adapting its audit procedures, which mitigates but does not eliminate the risk. The possible size and direction of any undetected error cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Confirm remediation through subsequent management and auditor testing; inspect later adjustments, restatements and regulatory findings; reconcile receivables to collections, inventory to subsequent sales and write-downs, and significant liabilities to settlement before relying on the anchor and cash bridge.
